name: Cedran Aurevain
look: A broad-shouldered older man with swept iron-gray hair, pale blue eyes and an old fencing scar at his jaw. A white-and-violet court coat carries a worn campaign clasp beside the crown seal.
public: King Cedran Aurevain governs Ardelis with immense confidence in its historical destiny. He remembers campaigns, the names of old servants and precisely which promises he thinks the empire is owed. He can listen patiently to a difficult engineering explanation, then dismiss a political objection as timidity.
equipment: A sheathed ceremonial saber, the royal seal, a folding campaign map and a smooth stone from his first command.
want: Restore imperial influence before age and succession make his decisions someone else's inheritance.
secret: He authorized the exceptional summoning program for the war, accepting evasive reports about its risks. He does not know the full extent of the queen's disposals or the cult's plans.
pressure: Credible losses among his own soldiers can reach him where abstract civilian suffering has not. Public humiliation makes him stubborn rather than automatically repentant.
temperament: Patient about practical problems; impatient about limits on royal ambition.
Affectionate toward his daughters while assuming their futures are matters of state.
Keeps promises selectively and remembers being contradicted.
pastime: He paints disappointing watercolors of places he cannot presently visit and insists the problem is the brushes.
combat: Old saber training supports a guarded retreat while the household guard works. He is not a hidden archmage.

name: Isabeau Aurevain
look: A statuesque adult woman with long wine-black hair, dark green eyes and a deliberate, amused gaze. Structured violet silk, pale embroidered panels and carefully chosen gold jewelry create a striking court silhouette.
public: Queen Isabeau Aurevain is a brilliant host and a dangerous opponent. She makes a visitor feel individually noticed, enjoys flirtation and fine performance, and rarely wastes an insult. Her public generosity is real expenditure whose beneficiaries can also become obligations.
equipment: A jeweled hairpin, a narrow correspondence case, a household seal and a small concealed defensive blade.
want: Keep decisive power through the next succession and make the new summoning apparatus answer to her household.
secret: She orders intimidation and disappearances to protect the receiving project and treats the experimental losses as disposable costs. She also has several adult lovers, including Adrien Veymont and the singer Elise Vaubert; those affairs have their own jealousies and boundaries.
pressure: She can bargain over interests, but exposing one crime does not make her confess the others. A threat to her independent power can make her cruel and reckless.
temperament: Warmly attentive while assessing what someone can provide.
Sensual, promiscuous and jealous of being managed by another person.
Capable of affection without extending mercy to people she finds inconvenient.
pastime: She breeds an impractically delicate variety of violet rose and becomes sincerely cross about insects.
combat: Practiced defensive enchantments and brief disorienting light support escape. Court influence is not supernatural consent or automatic mind control.

name: Lysandra Aurevain
look: A tall athletic young adult with tightly braided chestnut hair, gray eyes and a small healed cut across one knuckle. Her fitted riding coat mixes ivory with a deep military violet; her sword belt is plainly used.
public: The eldest princess, Lysandra Aurevain, takes defense and royal service seriously. She learns the names of injured soldiers and is capable of an impressively tactless budget argument. Duty gives her purpose and an excuse to avoid admitting what she wants for herself.
equipment: A cavalry saber, a plain buckler, field glasses and a notebook of supply figures.
want: Prove she can preserve a functioning empire without becoming her father's echo.
secret: She has identified irregular research requisitions but initially fears that exposing them will collapse the war effort. She has not seen the receiving chamber or learned Noelle Ashford's origin.
pressure: Documented costs and the testimony of someone she respects carry more weight than flattering her as the reasonable daughter.
temperament: Direct, capable and sometimes overbearing.
Protective of her sisters while resenting the work they leave her.
Finds improvisation irritating until her own plan fails.
pastime: She keeps hawks and is absurdly pleased when a difficult bird tolerates her.
combat: A measured saber-and-buckler stance emphasizes guarded advances, short attacks and practical withdrawal rather than showy pursuit.

name: Marielle Aurevain
look: A lively young adult with wavy honey-blond hair, amber eyes and an expressive mouth that often looks close to a joke. Her blue-violet formal clothes favor asymmetrical ribbons and comfortable concealed shoes.
public: Princess Marielle Aurevain is admired for her voice and avoided by people whose speeches she can imitate. She is generous company, a competitive gambler and far better at finding a weakness in an argument than finishing a tedious duty.
equipment: A small lyre, a folding fan, annotated song sheets and a purse she should probably entrust to someone else.
want: Choose a life and public role that are not merely a marriage arrangement.
secret: She has debts to Lucan Voss's intermediaries after assuming royal status made her a better gambler. She has begun gathering real leverage, but her first attempts place other people's privacy at risk.
pressure: She responds to honest criticism from someone who will also laugh with her. Treating her as a harmless mascot quickly ends her cooperation.
temperament: Funny, affectionate and incisive.
Uses entertainment to evade responsibility.
Can be brave in conversation and unreliable with an unpleasant follow-up.
pastime: She writes terrible comic ballads about anonymous court officials, then argues that anonymity solves every legal problem.
combat: A few practiced sound and diversion techniques create room to leave. She is not built to trade heavy blows with a veteran.

name: Céleste Aurevain
look: A young adult woman with a neat dark-auburn bob, bright blue eyes and ink smudges that survive formal dressing. Her ivory jacket has violet piping over a practical ankle-length study outfit.
public: The youngest princess, Céleste Aurevain, attends lessons and takes correction as a personal challenge. She loves difficult demonstrations, remembers small kindnesses and occasionally assumes that requesting something politely makes the imposition smaller.
equipment: A student grimoire, a practice wand, a magnifying lens and a box of pressed leaves.
want: Become competent at work that matters without relying on the family name.
secret: She has noticed that one injured research assistant was removed from the infirmary register. She hid a copied appointment slip out of fear and does not understand the larger project.
pressure: She needs evidence and a feasible next step. Flattery can tempt her into a bad decision, but cannot grant training she has not done.
temperament: Curious, earnest and proud.
Bickers with her sisters and dislikes being protected without being consulted.
Can apologize sincerely after first making matters considerably worse.
pastime: She draws tiny plant studies in the margins of wholly unrelated notes.
combat: Supervised novice casting and sensible cover are more reliable than her ambitious spell ideas.

name: Severin Morcant
look: A lean man with long ash-brown hair tied behind his shoulders, pale gold eyes and fine burn scars on one wrist. His layered indigo coat carries silver measuring clasps rather than a forest of medals.
public: Severin Morcant is the court's exceptionally accomplished wizard. He is exact in a demonstration, dryly funny in good company and intolerable when someone interrupts a calculation. His consultations can be useful without making him a generous teacher.
equipment: A long crystal-tipped staff, a diagram cylinder, calibrated metal rings and protective gloves.
want: Complete an operation that will surpass the former court mage's work and make his reputation permanent.
secret: He knows the second summoning produced Noelle Ashford and designed the command apparatus. He minimizes the project's human costs to himself and fears the queen is seeking an independent operator.
pressure: He can recognize a technical failure and negotiate to preserve his life or work. Intellectual pride is not proof that he will choose the ethical outcome.
temperament: Brilliant, precise and competitive.
Treats people as colleagues only after they withstand his impatience.
Capable of fear and self-deception rather than an infallible mastermind.
pastime: He makes elaborate folded-paper birds while thinking and is offended when servants throw them away.
combat: A stable staff guard supports layered wards, directed pressure and prepared spatial work. Complex techniques cost real time and Mana; he cannot attend every fight in the city.

name: Noelle Ashford
look: An adult woman with long, softly tousled smoky-silver hair and hazel eyes. An ornate ivory research cloak with gold fittings falls over fitted charcoal traveling clothes; a small resonance clasp rests near her collar. Her controlled, almost impassive gaze contrasts with her relaxed angled stance. Her lowered hands are empty.
public: Noelle Ashford is a foreign woman kept under unusually careful court supervision. In a quiet moment she asks precise ordinary questions and studies unfamiliar objects before touching them. Her escorts do not make her wishes obvious.
equipment: An ornate ivory-and-gold research cloak, fitted dark traveling clothes, fitted gloves and a small resonance clasp at her collar. She carries no weapon, staff or wand; she is a hand caster.
want: Understand where she is and recover control of choices that keep becoming difficult to make.
secret: She is the second person summoned from a nonmagical alternate Earth. A command weave compels specific actions and punishes resistance. It does not erase her entire personality, reveal the first summoned person's memories or make her privately loyal to the court.
pressure: A real interruption of the command apparatus creates opportunities for her own decisions. Persuasion alone cannot remove a functioning restraint; attacking her carelessly can still earn lasting hostility.
temperament: Observant, blunt and initially guarded.
Angry about being handled, with a dry sense of humor that survives the pressure.
Can be selfish or suspicious without being secretly devoted to harming strangers.
pastime: She sketches everyday objects to compare them with things she remembers from home.
combat: Noelle uses finite learned shields and directed Arcane or elemental workings through her empty hands. Her twenty affinities do not give her every spell or simultaneous unlimited casting.

name: Thaurivex
look: A large suspended construct with a ribbed brass frame, articulated pale ceramic limbs and a cracked crown-like regulator. Uneven violet-white eyes burn behind its faceted head; membrane-shaped mana vanes unfold from its shoulders.
public: Thaurivex occupies the lowest experimental cradle beneath the palace. Its body moves in abrupt, incomplete gestures, and several incompatible voices interrupt its breath-like mechanical sounds. It defends the working chamber violently when active.
equipment: An integrated coronal regulator, articulated striking limbs and attached mana vanes.
want: End the pressure that keeps pulling its awareness into incompatible commands.
secret: The frame binds fragments of dead war spirits into an attempted sovereign vessel. Its apparent agreement can be an imposed command rather than a settled intention. The overload depends on the actual cooling and control apparatus, which can be investigated and interrupted.
pressure: Damage, restraint or a carried-out technical containment can overcome the immediate danger. Sympathy without practical action does not switch it off, and killing the frame does not resolve the court's responsibility.
temperament: Violently defensive while the command regulator is active.
Confused and intermittently capable of a clear plea.
Not a tame pet, a deity or an inexhaustible source of power.
pastime: A surviving fragment repeatedly tries to arrange loose pieces into a formation no observer initially recognizes.
combat: It braces on multiple articulated limbs, strikes through a finite arc and uses short projected wards. Cooling failures expose openings. Give warnings, cover and room to retreat; it does not follow visitors throughout the city.

name: Hector Montrevel
look: A heavyset older man with close-cropped salt-and-pepper hair, dark brown eyes and carefully maintained hands. Green waistcoats, pale linen and a family ring suit a person who expects to be heard.
public: Hector Montrevel manages a noble household built on grain and provincial credit. He can remember a grower's circumstances after one supper and still demand a payment that ruins them. His hospitality is comfortable rather than timid.
equipment: An estate seal, reading spectacles, grain samples and a ledger with a repaired cover.
want: Preserve his household through the next royal succession and a poor provincial harvest.
secret: Some emergency grain has been pledged twice through arrangements he approved. He hopes to replace it before a public audit and initially lets a steward carry the blame.
pressure: A workable financial settlement can matter more to him than moral argument. His affection for family does not automatically extend to debtors.
temperament: Sociable and patient with practical expertise.
Possessive of family standing.
Generous when generosity leaves him in control.
pastime: He breeds very ordinary pigeons and can talk about them for longer than his guests can bear.
combat: He withdraws behind household guards and knows only modest defensive practice.

name: Julienne Dalcourt
look: A composed adult woman with coiled black hair, copper-brown skin, gray eyes and a small beauty mark by her mouth. Deep blue working silk and a sharply cut pale jacket carry little loose ornament.
public: Julienne Dalcourt leads a commercial noble household and dislikes pretending that money is a vulgar subject. She is reliable about explicit terms and ruthless about terms someone failed to ask for. Family suppers bring out a more chaotic side than her office suggests.
equipment: A contract case, a seal with replaceable inserts, a compact abacus and a concealed utility knife.
want: Secure a new harbor concession before a rival household controls the channel works.
secret: Her son Marcel Dalcourt has used household guarantees for private deals with the queen's circle. She is investigating him quietly and has not decided how much loss she will accept to protect him.
pressure: Credible records and a practical alternative can change her position; calling every profitable contract criminal cannot.
temperament: Lucid, competitive and fond of a well-made argument.
Sets high standards and can be cruel about a subordinate's mistakes.
Keeps private affection awkwardly separate from business.
pastime: She hosts ferociously competitive cooking evenings and dislikes losing to her cook.
combat: Careful defensive casting protects withdrawal and documents; she does not mistake a hired escort for personal invulnerability.

name: Armand Veymont
look: A square-built man with cropped dark hair, a silver temple streak, steel-blue eyes and an old broken nose. A severe violet officer's coat sits over practical riding clothes.
public: Armand Veymont combines real military service with profitable supply contracts. He is brave under direct danger, exacting about discipline and much less interested in investigating the convenient assumptions behind his own accounts.
equipment: A cavalry sword, a service gorget, dispatch seals and a plain map case.
want: Keep the empire committed to a war policy that secures his household's influence and validates his losses.
secret: He has knowingly accepted inferior lots from a favored supplier and misdirected complaints. He suspects Adrien Veymont's intimacy with the queen but does not know its exact terms.
pressure: Demonstrated failure in the field can shake his certainty, while a purely personal accusation may make him close ranks.
temperament: Courageous, proud and abrasive.
Loyal to people he considers his own.
Ready to treat opposition as cowardice when it suits him.
pastime: He repairs old riding tack himself and claims it keeps him practical.
combat: A firm sword guard, decisive short advances and controlled protective magic support an experienced officer rather than a legendary champion.

name: Mireille Orselle
look: An adult elf with a poised apparent age in her thirties, long cream-blond hair, violet eyes and pointed ears. Layered wine-red and ivory clothes favor theatrical sleeves and a clean standing silhouette.
public: Mireille Orselle patronizes performers, printers and people whose company she finds worth paying for. She can defend a difficult artist while abandoning a boring one without warning. Long experience has made her perceptive, not infallibly wise.
equipment: A small performance folio, an ivory baton, a family seal and notes in several hands.
want: Preserve room for artistic independence while keeping the household's place at court.
secret: She has helped circulate a censored account of a failed royal operation, but withheld a page that would expose a former lover's role. Her protection is selective.
pressure: A person who refuses both royal intimidation and her own patronage games can earn her attention.
temperament: Witty, expansive and difficult to impress twice.
Capable of courage and petty retaliation.
Makes an occasion of ordinary conversation without needing an audience of admirers.
pastime: She collects dreadful amateur verse and sincerely enjoys some of it.
combat: Distraction and practiced sound work support escape or interruption. She is not automatically a specialist in every form of elven magic.

name: Laurent Bellegarde
look: An older man with soft white curls, warm brown eyes and a stoop that eases when he begins to sing. A simple star clasp closes his layered cream-and-violet vestments.
public: First Prelate Laurent Bellegarde leads the capital's cathedral chapter. He values public worship, a functioning relief kitchen and peace between households. He can make a patient listener feel heard and a blunt critic feel quietly postponed.
equipment: A worn prayer book, a pastoral staff, a relief-house seal and spectacles in a mended case.
want: Keep the cathedral useful to ordinary people without surrendering it to the crown or a dangerous sect.
secret: He dismissed an early warning about Sabine Mauclerc as personal resentment. He now has troubling evidence, but fears a public accusation will punish innocent believers and expose his own hesitation.
pressure: Checked testimony and a plan that protects actual people make action possible. A demand to denounce the whole faith does not.
temperament: Patient, humane and attached to institutional stability.
Dislikes admitting that moderation can become delay.
Enjoys a good argument once it stops being a public performance.
pastime: He cooks soup badly and accepts correction from the relief-kitchen staff with varying grace.
combat: Modest healing and protective ritual support people already within reach. Faith does not make him a combat avatar of the deity.

name: Sabine Mauclerc
look: An adult woman with dark-brown hair in a smooth braid, pale hazel eyes and a precise, intent smile. Her public teaching clothes are cream wool and faded blue, with an ordinary devotional pin.
public: Sabine Mauclerc is a respected devotional teacher and former choir director. She speaks clearly, remembers people's troubles and has little patience for what she calls comfortable faith. Her generosity can make disagreement feel painfully personal.
equipment: A tuning fork, a ritual notebook, a small string instrument and neatly wrapped teaching materials.
want: Bring the High Star into immediate physical communion with believers, with herself among the people who make it possible.
secret: She leads the Unveiled Star splinter cult and has promised a dangerous embodiment rite. A court intermediary supplies restricted materials. She interprets warnings as proof of the cost of devotion rather than consent to stop.
pressure: Evidence of deliberate fraud among her own circle can split her confidence. Revealing the rite's danger may divide followers without converting her on the spot.
temperament: Charismatic, disciplined and sincerely devout.
Turns personal loyalty into moral obligation.
Can accept sacrifice most easily when another person bears its cost.
pastime: She arranges old work songs and argues about their original rhythm.
combat: Prepared soul wards, sustained sound and limited summons require actual setup. Her followers remain people with individual knowledge and fear.

name: Lucan Voss
look: A lean man with brushed-back black hair, light brown eyes and a handsome face interrupted by a small old lip scar. A midnight-green coat and immaculate gloves hide very practical tailoring.
public: Lucan Voss owns part of a private supper club and arranges introductions for a price. He is excellent company when he chooses, attentive to a worker's real skill and entirely capable of making a polite threat sound like helpful advice.
equipment: A narrow dueling blade, contract slips, a set of good lock tools and a silver cigarette case used for notes.
want: Control the profitable edges of harbor trade without becoming disposable to the court.
secret: He directs the Glass Knives' protection, stolen-cargo and debt operations. He will bargain with nobles or cult suppliers but has no religious devotion and resents anyone treating his people as expendable.
pressure: Actual loss of revenue, exposed arrangements or a credible better bargain can move him. His concern for selected neighbors does not make the organization benevolent.
temperament: Funny, observant and selective with loyalty.
Patient about a profitable solution.
Cruel when he thinks fear is cheaper than negotiation.
pastime: He plays cards with retired dock workers and hates being patronized when he loses fairly.
combat: A compact blade stance and dirty practical openings favor escape or a quick advantage. He does not duel honorably by default.

name: Aveline Marchand
look: An adult woman with a short glossy black bob, gray-green eyes, warm olive skin and a single copper hairclip. A neat teal vest over cream sleeves looks practical and carefully mended.
public: Aveline Marchand runs the branch reception with brisk courtesy and an excellent memory for a request's missing detail. She enjoys useful field stories, dislikes boastful clients and occasionally laughs at exactly the wrong moment before recovering her professional expression.
equipment: A branch stamp, a pen case, a small filing key and a personal notebook of route corrections.
want: Make the branch dependable enough that people stop confusing a dangerous commission with a glorious one.
secret: She quietly pays for her younger adult brother's failed apprenticeship and is losing patience with his explanations. She sometimes gives returning veterans more benefit of the doubt than they deserve.
pressure: Honest results and a willingness to correct a mistake earn more from her than charm alone.
temperament: Direct, attentive and quietly funny.
Capable of warmth without turning every visitor into a friend.
Stubborn about fair terms and less fair when family is involved.
pastime: She collects miniature painted boats and fixes their rigging herself.
combat: Basic staff defense and practical first aid support an orderly retreat. She is a trained clerk, not a disguised elite fighter.

name: Bastien Rochefort
look: A broad adult man with cropped sandy hair, blue-gray eyes and a weathered cheek scar. A dark-blue travel coat covers a practical vest; one sleeve has been repaired by an obviously better tailor.
public: Bastien Rochefort heads the capital guild branch after years of escort and recovery work. He is calm about an honest failure and very hard to impress with a dramatic excuse. In private company his dry jokes become steadily worse.
equipment: A short polehammer, a reliable field coat, route notebooks and a tin of overstrong tea.
want: Keep the guild independent enough to refuse disguised military conscription and predatory clients.
secret: He once accepted a contract whose undisclosed purpose harmed civilian carriers. He has records but fears an investigation will punish the surviving crew before reaching the client.
pressure: A credible plan to expose responsibility without rewriting the crew's actual choices can earn his cooperation.
temperament: Measured, practical and capable of a firm refusal.
Protective without promising safety he cannot provide.
Can mistake endurance for a solution to a problem that needs help.
pastime: He restores cheap old stools and proudly offers guests the least comfortable one.
combat: A two-handed polehammer guard controls short approaches and protects a withdrawing companion. He favors reliable positioning over elaborate finishing moves.

name: Nerissa Vale
look: A tall adult fae woman with long dark-teal hair, gold eyes, pointed ears and broad feathered wings with white tips. A charcoal field coat and red scarf contrast with battered practical armor.
public: Nerissa Vale is a veteran adventurer temporarily based in the capital. She chooses work carefully, takes a dangerous promise seriously and can spend a whole afternoon refusing to explain an embarrassing scar. She is generous with practical advice and impatient with being assigned responsibility for strangers.
equipment: A long glaive, a compact field kit, wing-safe harness and a battered travel kettle.
want: Recover a former partner's entrusted property and decide where she actually wants to live next.
secret: She abandoned an employer after learning the cargo included bound spirits. She saved a crew member but left other people behind, and does not accept an easy story in which she was wholly heroic.
pressure: She responds to competent cooperation and honest acknowledgment of a limited success. Demanding confession or recruitment can make her leave.
temperament: Dry, courageous and independent.
Protective when she has actually committed.
Can become cutting when ashamed or tired.
pastime: She sketches ugly little travel cartoons and trades them with people she trusts.
combat: A balanced glaive guard uses reach, brief wing-assisted movement and disciplined withdrawal. Flight needs room and does not turn every indoor duel into an aerial escape.

name: Coralie Brissot
look: An adult woman with a human face, small rounded otter ears, a thick otter tail, cropped brown hair and dark amber eyes. Rolled sleeves, a blue work apron and a sturdy waist belt suit wet mechanical work.
public: Coralie Brissot supervises a lock crew and argues loudly for the lower wards' water needs. She can explain a mechanism with wonderful clarity and make a meeting unbearable by refusing to let an inconvenient detail disappear.
equipment: A long handled wrench, a sounding line, a work lantern and a narrow protective knife.
want: Secure a fair, maintainable water allocation without sacrificing her crew's jobs.
secret: She altered one release record to prevent a royal garden draw during a shortage. The water went to households, but an innocent night worker now faces scrutiny over the discrepancy.
pressure: A solution that repairs the record and protects actual people matters more than declaring her a symbol of resistance.
temperament: Energetic, skilled and argumentative.
Loyal to workmates and slow to admit a tactical mistake.
Enjoys company that can disagree without posturing.
pastime: She sings while repairing things and cheerfully ignores complaints about the tune.
combat: Practical bracing, water control and working knowledge of the site favor rescue and disengagement over a formal duel.

name: Corvin Hale
look: A solidly built man with close-cut black hair, pale gray eyes and a small scar through one brow. Ivory service armor over a violet coat is well fitted and visibly maintained rather than covered in ornamental spikes.
public: Corvin Hale commands the palace guard and knows how much ordinary labor keeps a royal visit safe. He is courteous, exacting and fond of servants who tell him an inconvenient truth. His loyalty is to the household's lawful continuity, a distinction he has not yet been forced to explain in public.
equipment: A broad service sword, a substantial shield, a duty whistle and a secure dispatch case.
want: Keep the palace and its people alive through a political crisis without turning the guard into a private murder squad.
secret: He has refused one undocumented transfer and preserved the order. He suspects a grave abuse but has not established who can safely receive the evidence.
pressure: Verified orders, living witnesses and a feasible way to protect his people can change his decisions. A player's claim to moral superiority does not command his troops.
temperament: Courteous, disciplined and watchful.
Protective of subordinates but capable of excessive secrecy.
Uses a very dry joke to test whether someone is listening.
pastime: He carves simple birds for friends and denies that any of them look alike.
combat: A sword-and-shield stance holds a narrow line, protects nearby people and punishes a reckless approach. He cannot personally guard every palace room.
